idiom_name: Play Cached action over AsyncCacheApi (Caffeine/Ehcache, Redis plugin for shared state)
implementation_notes: Play expresses the pattern as action composition: the injected Cached helper wraps an action and caches the produced Result under a key you choose - cached("homePage") { Action { ... } }, or a per-variant key such as cached(req => "profile." + userId) - and serves it on a hit without running the action body, which Play's documentation explicitly permits because Result instances are safe to cache and reuse; cached.status(...).includeStatus(...) restricts caching to chosen status codes, and the store is the configured Play CacheApi (Caffeine in-process by default, Ehcache, or third-party memcached/Redis plugins when several nodes must share entries). This replaces the hand-written filter and store for the JVM's Scala stack; freshness and eviction stay your responsibility through cache.set/getOrElseUpdate/remove with durations.
pitfalls: getOrElseUpdate is get-then-set on some providers (Play documents this for Ehcache), so a cold popular page can be rendered concurrently several times - a stampede rather than a correctness bug, but it shows up under load.
The default Caffeine store is per node: without a shared cache plugin a multi-node deployment serves different versions of the page from different nodes.
Keys must carry the personalisation axes: caching a per-user page under a constant key is the classic leak, and Play's key function is the place to prevent it.
